title: 中国国家罕见病目录 别名层 (alias layer for China's national rare disease lists)

provenance.builder: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-baozhiwei/ce303ed3-75bf-490b-aaab-d78c0511c5cb/scratchpad/cn/build_china_aliases.py; belongs in tools/china_list/ (that directory is outside this work package)

china_lists.licence: official PRC government publications (国卫医发〔2018〕10号, 国卫医政发〔2023〕26号); see that file's provenance
china_lists.note: names used exactly as published; this alias layer never alters them

orphanet_en_bulk.note: ORPHAcode + English 'Preferred term' only; no synonyms, hence the per-code detail calls. 11645 distinct normalised terms.

orphanet_zh_bulk.note: Orphanet's Chinese dataset is dated 2020-06-01, i.e. older than the 第二批 list (2023); 10563 rows collapse to 10528 distinct normalised terms, so a Chinese preferred term can be ambiguous.

orphanet_detail.note: per-ORPHAcode 'Preferred term', 'Synonym' and 'DisorderGroup'. 298 detail records attempted for the 149 linked codes in both languages (2 returned HTTP 404 on ?lang=zh, hence rows=296), plus 219 English records for the rule-d candidate codes. Requests paced >=0.25s apart and cached on disk. DisorderGroup across linked codes: {"Disorder": 116, "Group of disorders": 29, "Subtype of disorder": 4}.

mondo_zh.licence: Mondo CC-BY-4.0; served via EBI OLS4
mondo_zh.note: RECORDED NEGATIVE RESULT: no Chinese disease labels retrievable. HTTP 200 for all 7 distinct Mondo terms probed (MONDO:0011122, MONDO:0001056, MONDO:0010679, MONDO:0007193, MONDO:0001516, MONDO:0007113, MONDO:0019019; the China-list ones — spinal muscular atrophy, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Angelman syndrome, osteogenesis imperfecta — were resolved by OLS4 exact search), and a scan of every string in each full term record (label, synonyms, obo_synonym, annotations, descriptions) found 0 CJK characters. Mondo carries no zh translations in OLS4, so no Chinese alias was taken from it.

hpo_zh.note: RECORDED NEGATIVE RESULT: no Chinese disease labels retrievable. URL is the ZH_URL constant in zebra/hpo_local.py. HTTP 200, 18988 rows, every subject_id prefix is HP ({"HP": 18988}) and 0 rows reference an OMIM/ORPHA/MONDO id: this file translates PHENOTYPE terms, not diseases, so no Chinese disease alias was taken from it.

rules: a. exact: normalised name_en == an English Orphanet preferred term
b. exact: a '/'- or bracket-separated part of name_en == an English Orphanet preferred term
c. exact: normalised name_zh (or one of its '/'/bracket parts) == a Chinese Orphanet preferred term (zh dataset 2020-06-01)
c-tiebreak. when rule c hits several ORPHAcodes sharing one Chinese preferred term, the tie is broken only by an exact English preferred term or synonym among them; otherwise the entry is left null

d. exact: name_en (or one of its '/'/bracket parts) == an English Orphanet SYNONYM, checked only for the best difflib candidates of entries no earlier rule linked (candidates give a reason to fetch; the match itself is exact)
no link is ever made on fuzzy/approximate similarity: an entry no exact rule links keeps orpha=null and is listed in provenance.unmatched_list_entries
folk names are hand-entered, carry kind=folk_name + maps_to + a source saying so, and were each verified to map to a published name_zh in china_rare_diseases.json
notes: counts.aliases counts every alias object in the file, folk names included (counts.folk_names of them).

orpha_disorder_group is Orphanet's own English classification: 'Disorder' / 'Group of disorders' / 'Subtype of disorder'. A 'Group of disorders' code carries no genes in Orphanet, which matters downstream.
Chinese preferred terms and synonyms come from Orphanet's 2020-06-01 Chinese dataset and are therefore older than the 第二批 list (2023-09-18).
aliases are deduplicated on (text, kind); the same text can legitimately appear under two kinds (e.g. an Orphanet synonym that is also a folk name).

official_part_zh / official_part_en hold the '/'- or bracket-separated parts of the published name. 8 such fragments were reviewed and dropped because they are qualifiers or word-internal glosses rather than alternative disease names (a length or substring heuristic was not used, because it would also discard the genuine short names 脆骨病, 白塞病, 大动脉炎, HAE, LAM): 1/35 'I型、II型': severity/type qualifier of 糖原累积病, not a disease name; 1/35 'Type I、II': severity/type qualifier of Glycogen Storage Disease, not a disease name; 1/87 '青年型、早发型': onset qualifier of 帕金森病, not a disease name; 1/87 'Young-onset , Early-onset': onset qualifier of Parkinson Disease, not a disease name; 2/18 '冷吡啉': protein name (cryopyrin) glossed inside the disease name, not a disease name; 2/18 '冷炎素': the inline gloss of 冷吡啉 (cryopyrin), a protein name, not a disease name; 2/18 '相关周期性综合征': dangling remainder left after the inline gloss is split out, not a disease name; 2/78 '重型': severity qualifier of 地中海贫血, not a disease name

tie-breaks applied: 1/22 先天性肌强直（非营养不良性肌强直综合征） -> left null: ORPHA:614, ORPHA:206973 share the Chinese preferred term '先天性肌强直' and none of them carries an English preferred term or synonym equal to 'Congenital Myotonia Syndrome (Non-Dystrophic Myotonia, NDM)', so no exact rule can choose between them

2 linked codes have no orphanet_zh / orphanet_synonym_zh alias because the Orphanet zh endpoint returns HTTP 404 for them (codes newer than the 2020-06-01 Chinese dataset): 1/9 自身免疫性脑炎 -> ORPHA:622014; 2/52 发作性睡病 -> ORPHA:619284

second builder pass (tools/china_list/add_folk_names.py) 2026-10-06 added 9 hand-entered folk names and Chinese transliterations (瑞特/雷特综合征 for Rett综合征 — the first pass left 瑞特综合征 matching 白塞病, the defect this layer exists to fix; 蝴蝶宝贝/蝴蝶宝宝, 黏宝宝/粘宝宝, 月亮孩子, 不食人间烟火的孩子, 玻璃人). Each is marked folk_name and names the official list entry it maps to; none comes from a retrieved dataset.
